input.prompt: Minimal sculptural still-life photograph, 16:9, calm museum atmosphere. Everything is one colour: pale Korean celadon green (#A9C4B5) - the back wall, the floor, a low rectangular plinth and the sculpture are all tinted the same celadon, tone-on-tone. On the plinth stands a thick, smooth plaster arch shaped like an upright half ring, and directly beneath the centre of the arch a perfect matte sphere floats in mid-air a few centimetres above the plinth, casting a soft round shadow - together they form a physical fermata, the musical sign for 'hold'. Chalky matte plaster with subtle pores; shadows deepen to a darker celadon (#6F9383). Soft diffused window light from the left, long gentle shadows to the right. The objects sit in the right 45% of the frame; the left 55% is an empty, evenly lit celadon wall reserved for typography. Eye-level camera, 70mm, sharp focus. No text, no logos, no other objects.
